title: WF03 EXT-01 stall removed at TC-EXT-01-INT-03; residual EXT-01 runtime/leak failures remain
summary: Resolved the residual EXT-01/OBS-05 integration failures by fixing service-task retry semantics for redirect responses, stabilizing EXT-01 integration harness startup/JSON assertions, and removing a service-task runtime allocation-lifetime leak path in completeTask processing.

root_cause.details: Remaining failures were caused by a combination of (1) redirect responses being classified as retriable and retried, (2) brittle EXT-01 integration assertions tied to serialized JSON text formatting, and (3) allocator-lifetime mismatch in service-task runtime state allocations during completeTask integration paths.

changes: Updated `src/engine/service_task.zig` to treat `http_redirect_3xx` as non-retriable so redirects fail immediately without retry loops or follow-on connection-refused side effects.
Updated `src/engine/instance.zig` to run service-task runtime allocations under the completeTask arena allocator, eliminating integration-path allocator lifetime leaks.
Updated `tests/integration/ext01_service_task_test.zig` with deterministic local-server readiness probing, robust JSON field assertions, and deterministic retriable-failure scenario behavior.
Updated `tests/integration/obs05_dlq_test.zig` pagination assertion to parse numeric count and assert non-empty next page behavior without brittle global-count assumptions.

commands.evidence: run completed with test database cleanup and exit code 0

prevention: For local test servers, always implement deterministic shutdown/wakeup so deferred joins cannot block forever when scenario requests are not observed.
Do not return DefinitionGraph slices backed by function-local runtime arrays; construct graph buffers in the same scope as immediate create/validate call usage.
Avoid brittle JSON substring assertions in integration tests; parse JSON and assert object fields semantically.
When paginated API tests run in a shared integration database, assert pagination behavior (cursor progression/non-empty pages) instead of hard-coding global list counts.
